polityNote: Republic of Armenia from the dissolution of the USSR (26 Dec 1991) to the eve of the law on administrative-territorial division (adopted 7 Nov 1995, signed 4 Dec 1995), from which the present-day record carries the ten marzer and Yerevan back. In this window the first-level units were the Soviet raions (37) and cities of republican subordination (22 in 1987, 23 in the 1995 Factbook). NOTHING IS DRAWN: the only finer atoms, geoBoundaries ARM ADM2 (labelled "2020, OCHA, municipal communities", 39 polygons), are in fact a raion layer of uncertain date — their names are the Soviet/1990s raions (Spitak, Gugark, Tashir, Ashotsk, Karmir, Dilidjan, Tavush) — and (1) every city of republican subordination is merged into a raion polygon (point tests: Gyumri in Akhuryan, Vanadzor in Gugark, Abovyan in Kotayk, Hrazdan and Charentsavan in Hrazdan, Ejmiatsin in Vagharshapat, Jermuk in Vayk, Alaverdi in Tumanian, Kapan in Kapan, Dilijan in Dilidjan, Sevan in Sevan); (2) their areas disagree with the 1991 raion areas of the Atlas of Armenia (statoids.com/uam.html) by up to 40% (Aparan 505 km2 vs 816, Ashtarak 674 vs 932, Armavir/Hoktemberyan 413 vs 701, Ijevan 1,003 vs 1,299, Talin 1,097 vs 1,288, Artik 525 vs 634), and the set has Masis and Dilijan raions the 1991 list lacks while lacking Vedi; (3) they leave 6.8% of the country outline uncovered (Lake Sevan and edges). A union of them would claim lines nobody has dated.
